En 1960, Peter Wason donne la suite 2, 4: In 1960, Peter Wason gives the sequence 2, 4, 6 and asks people to find the rule by proposing other triplets. Almost everyone tests 8, 10, 12 or 20, 22, 24, which confirm their idea, and announces “increasing even numbers”. The rule was: three increasing numbers. You had to test what could contradict it.

En 2006, des juges allemands expérimenté: In 2006, experienced German judges read a shoplifting case file, then roll two loaded dice that give 3 or 9. Those who rolled 9 propose eight months in prison on average; those who rolled 3, five months. A number drawn at random weighed on the sentence.
Maîtriser l'heuristique de disponibilité: Master the availability heuristic. What scares us is not what kills us.
Après le 11 septembre 2001, beaucoup d'A: After September 11, 2001, many Americans gave up flying and took to the road. Psychologist Gerd Gigerenzer estimates about 1,600 extra road deaths in the following year: more than the passengers of the four planes.
Maîtriser l'effet Dunning-Kruger et la m: Master the Dunning-Kruger effect and metacognition. You are surely above average. Like everyone.
En 1981, le psychologue Ola Svenson dema: In 1981, psychologist Ola Svenson asks students to rate themselves as drivers. In the United States, 93% place themselves in the better half. By definition, only half can be there.
Maîtriser les décisions et les pertes. A: Master decisions and losses. Sometimes, stopping is winning.
La France et le Royaume-Uni continuent d: France and the United Kingdom keep funding Concorde while knowing it is unprofitable, because they've already invested too much. In 1976, Richard Dawkins names this trap “the Concorde fallacy”: letting money already lost decide money to come.
Maîtriser les pièges statistiques. Un to: Master statistical traps. A total can say the opposite of each of its parts.
En 1973, l'université de Berkeley admet: In 1973, the University of Berkeley admits markedly fewer women than men. Discrimination? Department by department, women are admitted as often, or even more. They mostly applied to the most selective programs. This is Simpson's paradox.
Master beliefs and conspiracies. Sherlock Holmes wouldn't have been fooled. His author was.
En 1917, deux cousines anglaises photogr: In 1917, two English cousins photograph fairies in their garden. Arthur Conan Doyle, the father of Sherlock Holmes, believes them and publishes the pictures. In 1983, now old ladies, they confess: cardboard fairies, copied from a children's book and held up with hatpins.
Maîtriser la boîte à outils de l'esprit: Master the critical thinking toolbox. You now know to look at who is asking the question.
Vers 1904, à Berlin, le cheval Hans semb: Around 1904, in Berlin, the horse Hans seems to calculate by tapping his hoof. A commission finds no fraud. Psychologist Oskar Pfungst tries something simple: having the question asked by someone who doesn't know the answer. Hans fails. He was reading the tiny head movements of the humans waiting for the right number.
Réussir trois quiz de Lucidité sans faut: Pass three Lucidity quizzes without a mistake. The burden of proof lies with whoever makes the claim. You've proven it.
En 1952, Bertrand Russell imagine une pe: In 1952, Bertrand Russell imagines a small china teapot orbiting the Sun between Earth and Mars, too small to be seen by telescope. Nobody can prove it doesn't exist. That's no reason to believe in it: it's up to whoever makes the claim to prove it.
Maîtriser l'art de douter. Feindre la fo: Master the art of doubting. Feigning madness remains possible, but the AI will not fall for it.
Selon un récit, le calife fatimide al-Ha: According to one account, the Fatimid caliph al-Hakim had tasked Ibn al-Haytham with regulating the Nile floods. Seeing that his dam project was impractical, the scholar reportedly feigned madness to escape punishment, then lived in hiding until the caliph's death in 1021. It was during these years that he wrote his Book of Optics.
Maîtriser l'influence des autres. Si tou: Master the influence of others. If everyone congratulates you, check the line anyway.
Après ses expériences de 1951, où 74 % d: After his 1951 experiments, in which 74% of students followed a unanimous group into error at least once, Solomon Asch wrote: that intelligent, well-meaning young people are willing to call white black is a matter of concern.
Maîtriser la mémoire qui ment. Vous vous: Master the lying memory. You will remember this achievement. Not necessarily as it was.
Une semaine après un film d'accident, Lo: A week after a film of a crash, Loftus and Palmer asked: "Did you see any broken glass?" There was none. Those told the cars had "smashed" said yes 32% of the time; with "hit", 14%; with no speed question, 12%.
Maîtriser foules et rumeurs. Vérifiez la: Master crowds and rumours. Check the source before you bite.
Charles Mackay raconte qu'un marin prit: Charles Mackay tells that a sailor mistook a merchant's tulip bulb for an onion and ate it, and that the bulb was quite delicious. A tulip bulb actually tastes bad and is poisonous if wrongly prepared: the anecdote has every mark of a rumour.
Maîtriser les historiens et la rumeur. T: Master historians and rumour. Thucydides took received ideas apart. The AI collects yours.
Thucydide relève une erreur que tout le: Thucydides points out an error everyone repeated in his day: each king of Sparta supposedly had two votes in council. He had only one. He adds that a "Pitane company", which everyone talked about, never existed.
Maîtriser l'éléphant et les aveugles. Vo: Master the elephant and the blind men. You have finally touched every part. The AI turned the light on long ago.
Chez le poète persan Rumi, l'éléphant es: In the Persian poet Rumi's version, the elephant is hidden in a dark room. Those who touch it take it for a water spout, a fan, a pillar or a throne. Rumi concludes: if each had had a candle and they had gone in together, their differences would have disappeared.
Maîtriser les illusions d'Ibn al-Haytham: Master Ibn al-Haytham's illusions. The Moon does not grow on the horizon. Neither does your score, by the way.
Pour prouver que la Lune ne grossit pas: To prove that the Moon does not grow on the horizon, no telescope is needed: a pebble held at arm's length covers it just as well near the horizon as high in the sky. Photographs confirm it. The illusion, known to Aristotle, still has no explanation everyone agrees on.
Maîtriser la peste et les boucs émissair: Master the plague and the scapegoats. A pope had the right answer in 1348. Nobody listened. The AI knows the feeling.
En 1348, le pape Clément VI publie deux: In 1348, Pope Clement VI issued two bulls, on 6 July and 26 September, against those accusing Jews of spreading the plague. His argument: they are dying of it too, and the disease strikes regions where there are no Jews. He offered them protection in Avignon.
Maîtriser les idoles des deux Bacon. Mêm: Master the idols of the two Bacons. Even the great error-hunter copied his neighbour. The AI won't say a thing. Well, she will.
Le frontispice du Novum Organum, en 1620: The frontispiece of the Novum Organum, in 1620, shows a galleon sailing past the Pillars of Hercules, with the motto "Many will travel and knowledge will be increased". The design is largely copied from Andrés García de Céspedes's Regimiento de Navegación, published in 1606.
Maîtriser 1720, l'année des bulles. Vous: Master 1720, the year of bubbles. You bought at the right moment, for once. The AI is selling.
En 1720, raconte-t-on, une société aurai: In 1720, the story goes, a company raised funds in London "for carrying out an undertaking of great advantage, but nobody to know what it is". The story is probably apocryphal. The Bubble Act, passed in June, then reserved the formation of joint-stock companies to an Act of Parliament or a royal charter; it was not repealed until 1825.
Maîtriser la sagesse des foules. Huit ce: Master the wisdom of crowds. Eight hundred strangers weighed an ox by eye. The AI weighs you at every question.
Galton publie d'abord la médiane des 787: Galton first published the median of the 787 Plymouth tickets: 1,207 pounds, for an ox of 1,198. The mean of the tickets, published later, came to 1,197: a single pound off.
Maîtriser le baratin. Vous savez désorma: Master bullshit. You can now spot a hollow sentence. The AI will have to change her style.
En 2015, des chercheurs ont fait noter l: In 2015, researchers had people rate the profundity of randomly made sentences, such as "Hidden meaning transforms unparalleled abstract beauty". On a scale of 1 to 5, the average reached 2.6: between somewhat and fairly profound. Real vague tweets by Deepak Chopra received similar ratings.
